m:rynek: The square is free and always open. St Mary's Basilica can be visited with a 20 zł ticket (about €4.60; reduced 10 zł): Monday–Saturday 11:30am–6pm, Sunday and holidays 2–6pm (mariacki.com). Veit Stoss's great wooden altarpiece usually opens at 11:50am (2:10pm on Sundays). You enter from the south side, not the main door on the square, and visits stop during services. The tower climb is seasonal and paid separately (about 20 zł, same-day only on site): check mariacki.com. The Christmas market on the square usually opens at the end of November (2026 dates to be checked).
m:sukiennice: National Museum (MNK): open Tuesday–Sunday 10am–6pm, closed on Mondays; last entry 20 minutes before closing. Ticket 35 zł (reduced 25 zł, about €8); 1 zł for young people aged 7 to 26 (mnk.pl). The website reported early closing at noon on 9 October 2026 and the lift out of service. No restoration notice for 2026–2027 on the page I read.
m:sotterr: Hours: Monday 10am–7pm, Tuesday 10am–3pm, Wednesday and Thursday 10am–7pm, Friday–Sunday 10am–8pm; last entry 75 minutes before closing. Closed on the second Monday of the month. Ticket 45 zł (reduced 35 zł, about €10), online at bilety.mhk.pl; on Tuesdays entry is free, but tickets are only collected at the desk and are limited (maximum 5 per person). The Kraków Museum website lists closures on 12 October, 1, 9, 11, 16, 17 and 18 November and 24 and 25 December (also the 14th: November or December, check); the years aren't written, but the dates match 2026.
m:wawel: The courtyard and the hill are free to visit. Castle (wawel.krakow.pl, tickets with an entry time): floors 1 and 2 with audio guide 95 zł (about €21.70; reduced 71 zł), a single floor 57 zł, Crown Treasury or Armoury 47 zł each. Open Tuesday–Sunday 9am–5pm; on Mondays it opens 10am–4pm with free, limited entries only. The Cathedral, the Sigismund bell and the royal tombs cost 26 zł (reduced 18 zł, about €5.90): Monday–Saturday 9am–4:30pm, Sunday 12:30–4:30pm, closed during masses (katedra-wawelska.pl). The Dragon's Den is only open until 31 October (15 zł). On 1 November the castle is closed. Tickets online up to a month ahead at bilety.wawel.krakow.pl.
m:planty: The passage and the Planty are free. The Barbican and the defensive walls (Kraków Museum) are open Tuesday–Sunday 10am–4pm, closed on Mondays; ticket 22 zł (about €5). The rooms inside are among the smallest in the city: 20 minutes is enough.
m:czart: Pijarska street 15. Open Tuesday–Sunday 10am–6pm, closed on Mondays; last entry an hour before closing. Ticket 65 zł (reduced 50 zł, about €14.80; 1 zł for young people aged 7 to 26) with date and time, online at bilety.mnk.pl. On Tuesdays entry to the permanent collections is free, with limited tickets collected at the desk. Audio guide 15 zł. No restoration closure notice on the page I read.
m:kazimierz: The streets are free to walk. Old Synagogue (Szeroka 24, Kraków Museum): Monday 10am–3pm with free entry, Tuesday–Sunday 9am–5pm; last entry 30 minutes before closing. Ticket 22 zł (reduced 16 zł, about €5). Closed on 8 October, 1, 11 and 12 November, 10, 24, 25 and 31 December and on Jewish holidays (dates from muzeumkrakowa.pl, without the year). Synagogues still in use, like the Remuh, have their own hours and prices that I didn't check: they're closed to visitors during services and usually on Saturdays, check first. Be respectful: speak quietly, cover shoulders and knees inside places of worship.
m:schindler: Lipowa street 4. Open Monday 10am–3pm (free entry, limited tickets at the desk only) and Tuesday–Sunday 9am–8pm; last entry an hour and a half before closing. Closed on the first Tuesday of the month (3 November and 1 December), on 1 and 11 November and on 24 and 25 December; on 18 December it closes at 2pm, on the 26th it opens 10am–6pm, on the 31st 10am–3pm. Ticket 60 zł (reduced 45 zł, about €13.70): buy online up to 90 days ahead (sales close 6 hours before the visit), with ID if the ticket is in your name. The desk only sells tickets for the first free slot of the day. The website gives no minimum age: think carefully about bringing young children.
m:ghetto: The square is always accessible and free: it's a place of remembrance, behave respectfully. The Under the Eagle Pharmacy (Plac Bohaterów Getta 18, Kraków Museum) is open Wednesday–Sunday 9am–5pm, closed Monday and Tuesday; ticket 22 zł (about €5), free on Wednesdays. Closed on 1 and 11 November and 24, 25, 26 and 31 December.
vd:jama: A historic 1895 café near the Florian Gate, with Art Nouveau rooms full of paintings and decorations, famous for its cakes and the early-20th-century artists' cabaret. A place for breakfast or a slice of cake, not a quick meal.
vp:jama: A coffee with cake usually costs 35–50 zł (€8–11) and a dish of the day 45–70 zł (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:endzior: One of the kiosks in the Plac Nowy rotunda in Kazimierz, where you eat «zapiekanka»: half a toasted baguette with mushrooms, cheese and sauces. The city's most typical street food, eaten standing up.
vp:endzior: A zapiekanka usually costs 15–25 zł (€3.50–6) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:hawelka: A historic restaurant on the main square, open since the 19th century, with traditional Polish cooking: soups, pierogi, cutlets and stews. One of the few places on the Rynek that doesn't live only on tourists, but it's the priciest on the list.
vp:hawelka: A main course usually costs 55–90 zł (€12.50–20) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:starka: A Polish restaurant in the heart of Kazimierz, with home-style dishes like pierogi, bigos, cutlets and sour rye soup, and the aged vodka it's named after. A warm room and a relaxed atmosphere.
vp:starka: A main course usually costs 45–75 zł (€10–17) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:hevre: A place set in a former Jewish prayer hall, on a quiet street in Kazimierz: painted walls, a vaulted ceiling and a menu of Polish and Mediterranean dishes. Good for an unhurried dinner.
vp:hevre: A main course usually costs 45–75 zł (€10–17) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:mleczarnia: A café-restaurant in the Jewish quarter, with an outdoor courtyard and an old-house atmosphere: breakfasts, cakes, soups and simple Polish dishes. Good at any time, but the sunny courtyard is best from spring to October.
vp:mleczarnia: A breakfast or a soup with bread usually costs 25–45 zł (€6–10) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:camelot: A historic café a short walk from the Rynek, with vaulted rooms, dark wood and candles: Polish breakfasts, homemade cakes and tea. A nice place even on your own, with a book.
vp:camelot: A coffee with cake usually costs 30–45 zł (€7–10) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:aniolami: A restaurant in the medieval cellars of Grodzka street, halfway between the Rynek and Wawel: old-style Polish cooking, with grilled meats, duck and soups, in stone-vaulted rooms.
vp:aniolami: A main course usually costs 60–100 zł (€14–23), among the priciest on the list (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
vd:bunkier: A café with a terrace inside the Bunkier Sztuki, the modern art gallery on the edge of the Planty park, a few steps from the Rynek: breakfasts, sandwiches, cakes and a quiet corner to rest.
vp:bunkier: A coffee with cake usually costs 30–45 zł (€7–10) (estimate, menu not seen). Address and hours not checked: to be confirmed.
cd:wieliczka: A medieval mine with chapels, statues and underground lakes carved in salt, with a guided tour.
cx:wieliczka: It's 14 km from the centre: allow about 30 extra minutes by train or bus each way.
cd:muratusz: A free-standing tower on the Rynek, with a view over the square.
cx:muratusz: Open only in spring and summer: check the calendar.
cd:museonaz: Polish art from the Middle Ages to the 20th century and historic weapons.
cd:collegium: The oldest college of the Jagiellonian University, where Copernicus studied, with the professors' hall.
cd:mocak: Contemporary art in the former Schindler factory area.
cd:wislacruise: An hour by boat below Wawel and along the river.
cd:zoocracow: The zoo in Wolski Forest, with animals from every continent.
cd:kosciuszko: The hill with the 19th-century fort: the best view of Kraków and the Tatras.
